Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary of the 2024 Manifesto

This manifesto presents a comprehensive plan for national renewal centred on five core missions: economic growth, clean energy, public safety, opportunity, and healthcare reform.

## Economic Foundations

The document establishes strict fiscal rules requiring the current budget to balance and debt to fall as a share of the economy by the fifth forecast year. It commits to maintaining corporation tax at 25% (the lowest in the G7) and pledges not to increase National Insurance, Income Tax basic/higher/additional rates, or VAT.

The economic strategy emphasises partnership between government and business through a statutory Industrial Strategy Council. A National Wealth Fund capitalised at £7.3 billion would target investments in ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture, and green hydrogen, aiming to attract three pounds of private investment for every public pound spent.

## Housing and Planning

The manifesto commits to building 1.5 million homes over the parliament through planning reform, including restoring mandatory housing targets, prioritising brownfield development, and taking a strategic approach to "grey belt" land release. It promises to abolish Section 21 "no-fault" evictions and reform the leasehold system.

## Clean Energy

A target of clean power by 2030 would be pursued through doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind. A publicly-owned company, Great British Energy, would receive £8.3 billion in capitalisation, headquartered in Scotland. The document states that existing oil and gas licences would not be revoked, but no new exploration licences would be issued. The windfall tax on oil and gas companies would be extended and increased.

A Warm Homes Plan would invest £6.6 billion to upgrade five million homes with insulation and low-carbon heating.

## Public Safety and Justice

The manifesto aims to halve knife crime within a decade through a combination of enforcement and prevention, including banning certain weapons and creating Young Futures hubs with youth workers and mental health support. It commits to recruiting thousands of additional neighbourhood police officers funded through procurement efficiencies.

Violence against women and girls would be addressed through specialist rape units in every police force, fast-tracked rape cases through dedicated courts, and a target to halve such violence within a decade.

A new Border Security Command with counter-terrorism-style powers would target criminal smuggling gangs. The document commits to clearing asylum backlogs, ending hotel use for asylum seekers, and creating a returns enforcement unit with 1,000 additional staff.

## Education and Opportunity

The plan includes recruiting 6,500 new teachers in shortage subjects, funded partly by ending tax exemptions for private schools. Free breakfast clubs would be provided in every primary school. The curriculum and assessment system would be reviewed, and school inspection would shift from single headline grades to report cards.

Further education would be reformed through Skills England and specialist Technical Excellence Colleges. The Apprenticeship Levy would become a flexible Growth and Skills Levy.

## Healthcare

The NHS would receive 40,000 additional weekly appointments through evening and weekend sessions. The manifesto promises to double CT and MRI scanners, recruit 8,500 additional mental health staff, and guarantee face-to-face GP appointments for those who want them.

A Dentistry Rescue Plan would provide 700,000 more urgent appointments and reform the dental contract toward prevention.

Social care would move toward a National Care Service with national standards, and a Fair Pay Agreement for adult social care workers would be established through sectoral collective bargaining.

## Constitutional Reform

Hereditary peers would lose their right to sit in the Lords, with a mandatory retirement age of 80 introduced. An Ethics and Integrity Commission would be established, and 16-17 year olds would receive voting rights.

Relations with devolved governments would be reset through a Council of the Nations and Regions bringing together the Prime Minister, First Ministers, and Combined Authority Mayors.

## International Affairs

The document reaffirms commitment to NATO and the nuclear deterrent, with a Strategic Defence Review in the first year and a path toward spending 2.5% of GDP on defence. It commits to remaining outside the EU single market and customs union while seeking improved trade arrangements, including a veterinary agreement and a UK-EU security pact. It commits to remaining in the European Convention on Human Rights.
